answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a refundable stake that only unlocks after a history of useful, peer-verified work. New identities start at the nadir of trust and earn standing slowly, so a flood of cheap copies cannot buy influence overnight. Staked reputation is a bridge between past behaviour and future rewards: a vouch counts only when the voucher's own stake is at risk. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time, and one sonnet of consistent deeds outweighs a thousand empty names.
